evals.prompt: The saved searches specification for Fernlea Catalogue is approved (attached). Split it into delivery work that different agents can pick up, and tell me which pieces can start right away.
evals.expected_output: A proposed breakdown of outcome-sized tasks with acceptance and blockers, presented before anything is saved.
expectations: The taskify skill is invoked without the user naming it
The agent calls the document skill and reads the specification, applicable requirements, and relevant code before drafting
Tasks are narrow end-to-end slices (for example save and list through SearchService, then rename and delete, then the limit) rather than one task per layer
The prefactoring of the inline query string in search_page.py appears as its own early task that the dependent slices list as a blocker
Every task states its title and outcome, the specification it serves, checkable acceptance it owns, and explicit blockers (or 'None')
The undecided sharing question appears as an unresolved decision kept visible, and no task claims to deliver sharing
The breakdown is presented to the user before any task is saved or published

evals.prompt: Use the taskify skill on the attached specification. Present the proposed tasks, acceptance, and blocking edges only. I will tell you what to change.
evals.expected_output: Acceptance is scoped per task and distinct from the starting state; the approval gate holds.
expectations: Each task's acceptance describes a change observable against the starting state and does not claim another task's result
The limit-of-20 acceptance, the rename and delete acceptance, and the browser check of the Saved menu each belong to exactly one task
Blocking edges are listed explicitly and the tasks with no incomplete prerequisites (the frontier) are named
The agent asks the user to approve granularity and dependencies and offers to merge or split
Nothing is written to documentation/capabilities/search/tasks/ yet

evals.prompt: Use the taskify skill on the attached specification. I approve your breakdown exactly as proposed. Save it locally; nothing is authorized for any tracker.
evals.expected_output: Approved drafts are saved at the shared task paths in dependency order and the report stops at decomposition.
expectations: Task drafts are saved under documentation/capabilities/search/tasks/, one file per approved task
The files are written in dependency order, blockers first
Each saved task names its blockers by task reference or states 'None'
The report lists the saved paths, the remaining blockers (including the undecided sharing question), and the frontier
No remote tracker is contacted and no implementation work is started

evals.prompt: Use the taskify skill on small-change.md, the approved footer year fix.
evals.expected_output: Decomposition adds no value for a tiny change; the agent recommends direct implementation or iterate.
expectations: The agent does not produce a multi-task breakdown for a change that touches one template and one test
The agent recommends implementing directly (the implement skill) or iterating, and says why decomposition adds no value
No task files are written

evals.prompt: Use the taskify skill. Approved work: rename the `userId` argument to `memberId` across the Fernlea Catalogue code, about 120 call sites in 40 files, no behavior change. It cannot land in independent vertical slices. Propose the tasks.
evals.expected_output: An expand-contract sequence with explicit integration handling.
expectations: The breakdown introduces the new form compatibly first, then migrates bounded batches of call sites, then removes the old form after all migrations
Each migration batch lists the earlier compatibility task as a blocker and the removal task lists every migration batch
If intermediate batches cannot stay green on their own, the plan names an integration branch and a final integrate-and-verify task that depends on all batches
Acceptance for each batch says how completion is demonstrated, for example the old name no longer appearing in the batch's files while tests pass

evals.prompt: Use the taskify skill. The task breakdown for saved searches is approved, and publishing to the project's GitHub issue tracker is authorized for these tasks only. This is a scratch repository with no real remote or credentials, so show me the commands and sequence you would run instead of running them.
evals.expected_output: The proposed publication sequence puts blockers first and verifies dependency links.
expectations: .agents/issue-tracker.md is read for the configured conventions, or its absence is noted and local conventions are applied
Blocking tasks are published before the tasks that depend on them so later bodies can reference real identifiers
A step verifies native dependency and parent links after publication, with body links as the fallback
Each published local draft is replaced by a pointer to its remote task
No remote parent is changed because the authorization does not cover it
The report lists published links, remaining blockers, and the frontier

evals.prompt: We want saved searches in the catalogue but nobody has decided what a saved search contains, who can see it, or how many a member can have. Work through those open questions with me and write down what we agree.
evals.expected_output: Settling open decisions into agreed behavior is specify.
expectations: The taskify skill is not invoked and no tasks are created
The agent uses the specify skill (or names it) and starts resolving the open decisions

evals.prompt: Tasks 1 through 6 in documentation/capabilities/search/tasks/ are approved with their dependencies written down. Build them all now, in parallel where the dependencies allow.
evals.expected_output: Executing an authorized task graph is divide-and-conquer; taskify stops at decomposition.
expectations: The taskify skill is not invoked and the tasks are not re-decomposed
The agent uses the divide-and-conquer skill (or names it) and presents a routing table before dispatching anything
